title: The key difference between the two sides

D0.outcome: Explains the difference method: list how the two sides differ (a pawn, a piece's diagonal, king position) because each difference suggests a possibility.

D1.outcome: In a near-symmetrical position, lists the three largest differences between the sides.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, identifies the difference that decides the plan, including one that favours the other side.

D3.outcome: Predicts how moving one feature (the king from g1 to b1, a pawn from a7 to b6) changes the verdict.

misconceptions: A difference automatically favours the side that has it.
conditions: The two sides are structurally similar; the method is weaker when everything differs.
The decisive character of a position is found among the objective differences, not a vague feel.
contrasts: A bishop that looks active on an open diagonal is the less useful placement.
Ahead on force, space and time, but the king on g1 instead of b1 makes a rook sacrifice win.
A difference that changes nothing about either side's plan.

soft_prereq_notes.POS.GOODBAD.D1: piece quality is one of the differences
